condition.reason: macOS notifications are `UNUserNotificationCenter`, which needs a bundle identity to address and to hold permission against — and answers a process that has none by aborting it rather than by failing the call, so the facade cannot be installed and left to throw. An exported `.app` carries that identity and a development run of the interpreter does not; `blitsen run --dev-bundle` gives the development host one of its own rather than borrowing an installed application's. A process cannot acquire or lose a bundle identifier while it runs, so the question is settled once, as the runtime installs (#253). On Android the same question has a different subject: the facade's `click` is a body tap, and a body tap there is a `PendingIntent` addressed to an installed application identity, so a package the platform launched has one and a runtime started against a directory standing in for `assets/` does not — a `Notification` whose `onclick` could never fire would be a promise the constructor must not make (#252). `blitsen/notify` is present either way and says why a call was refused.

native.reason: A close request is a window event, and windows are issue #77's to expose; delivering one from here would mean a second, competing event loop.
Linux has no process-level suspend notification to report. The desktop portals that come closest describe the session, not this application.
The counterpart of `onSuspend`, absent for the same reason.

Registering `myapp://` on Linux means installing a `.desktop` entry that names the executable, which is what `blitsen build` already writes. A running process editing that entry would fight its own packaging. The activation itself arrives: the desktop launches the handler with the URL in `argv`, and the single-instance lock hands that to the instance already running.
The same `.desktop` entry, with `MimeType` instead of a scheme.

A second window needs the shared-versus-isolated JavaScript context question answered first: whether two windows see one `document` and one module graph or two decides what `create` even returns, and it cannot be settled by implementing it. The window this run already opened is what the rest of this module operates on.

Transparency is chosen when a window is created — winit's own setter does nothing on X11 after that — so honouring it would mean replacing the window, which is `create`. Run `blitsen` against a directory whose window should be transparent and the attribute belongs on that window, not on a call.

winit sets the window level and cannot read it back, and the window manager may change it without telling the application. Remembering what was last set would be a second source of truth that quietly goes stale.

Dropping *into* the window is winit's to report and is implemented; dragging *out* of it is not something winit can start. A drag source is a platform object driven from the thread that owns the window — `IDropSource` with `DoDragDrop`, an `NSDraggingSession`, a `wl_data_device` offer — and the first two run a modal loop that does not return until the drop, on the one thread Blitsen keeps free to paint. That is a design question rather than a missing call, so the module says so instead of answering it.

`arboard` reads the flavours above and no others. Arbitrary MIME needs a different mechanism on each platform — X11 selection targets, `wl_data_offer`, `NSPasteboardType`, a registered Windows format — and no part of that is shared.
The counterpart of `readMime`, absent for the same reason.
Gamepads need the standard navigator.getGamepads surface, stable device identity and hot-plug delivery; keyboard and pointer state alone cannot approximate them.
Vibration belongs to a discovered gamepad actuator and cannot be implemented before gamepad discovery identifies the device and its supported effects.
Device change is the connection counterpart of gamepad and raw-device discovery, neither of which is installed yet.
The monitors are `window.monitors()`, which already reports each one's size, position and scale factor. A second list here could disagree with that one.

Seconds since the last input is a different mechanism on every platform — the X11 screensaver extension, `CGEventSourceSecondsSinceLastEventType`, `GetLastInputInfo` — and Wayland has no answer at all for a client that is not focused: the idle-notify protocol reports crossing a threshold the compositor was asked about, not a duration. Reporting zero on the sessions that cannot answer would be indistinguishable from a machine in use. It is also the one reading in this module that describes the person rather than the machine — how long they have been away from the keyboard, available to any application that asks for it — so implementing it where it happens to work would buy that signal on three platforms in exchange for a wrong answer on the fourth.

WEB_INTL.message: This part of Intl is not implemented; the formatters are.
WEB_INTL.guidance: NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat — including named IANA time zones — RelativeTimeFormat, PluralRules, Collator and ListFormat are implemented over CLDR, and so are the `toLocale*` methods and `localeCompare` built on them. What is absent is the `formatToParts`/`formatRange` family, Segmenter, DisplayNames and DurationFormat: feature-detect them, or format the whole string and split it yourself.

WEB_WASM.message: WebAssembly is not implemented by the JavaScript engine Blitsen hosts.
WEB_WASM.guidance: Ship a JavaScript build of the module, or keep the work in a native addon.

WEB_DOM.message: This DOM method is not implemented.
WEB_DOM.guidance: Use the document-level lookups and node methods listed in COMPATIBILITY.md.

WEB_FORM_CONTROLS.message: This form-control API is not implemented.
WEB_FORM_CONTROLS.guidance: Validate and select in application code; handle the cancelable submit event rather than submitting the form.

WEB_SCHEDULING.guidance: Schedule the work with requestAnimationFrame or a timer.

WEB_STORAGE.guidance: Use a Node filesystem/database package, or the Web Storage APIs for session state.

WEB_WORKER.message: Shared and service workers are not implemented; dedicated Worker is.
WEB_WORKER.guidance: Use a dedicated Worker, which this runtime runs on a thread of its own, and keep whatever the workers were sharing in the document that started them.

WEB_MESSAGING.message: BroadcastChannel is not implemented; MessageChannel and Worker are.
WEB_MESSAGING.guidance: There is one document behind an application, so a channel between two of them has nothing to connect; pass a MessagePort to whoever needs one.

WEB_URL.message: Object URLs are not implemented; URL and URLSearchParams are.
WEB_URL.guidance: Pass the Blob itself to whatever was going to fetch the URL, or build a data: URL.

WEB_XHR.guidance: Use fetch with an absolute URL.

WEB_STREAM.message: Streaming bodies are not implemented; a response is buffered whole.
WEB_STREAM.guidance: Read the response with text(), json(), or arrayBuffer().

WEB_FORM.message: Multipart form bodies and file objects are not implemented.
WEB_FORM.guidance: Send a string, Blob, ArrayBuffer, or typed array body.

WEB_CANVAS.message: This canvas API is not implemented; the 2D context is.
WEB_CANVAS.guidance: Draw through getContext("2d"), and feature-detect anything that needs a second rendering target or a blur.

WEB_GPU.message: WebGL and WebGPU are not implemented.
WEB_GPU.guidance: Remove the GPU-web API path or replace it with a native addon/viewport.

WEB_MEDIA.message: This media API is not implemented; Web Audio and <audio> are.
WEB_MEDIA.guidance: Decode with AudioContext.decodeAudioData and play through a buffer source, or feature-detect the media path.

WEB_DIALOG.message: Modal browser dialogs are not implemented.
WEB_DIALOG.guidance: Use the native dialog module, or render the prompt as DOM.

WEB_NAVIGATION.message: Document navigation is deliberately absent; there is no page to leave.
WEB_NAVIGATION.guidance: Route with history.pushState and conditional DOM rendering.

WEB_COOKIE.message: There is no origin and no cookie jar behind an exported application.
WEB_COOKIE.guidance: Keep session state in memory or in a file the application owns.

WEB_DEVICE.message: This device API is not implemented.
WEB_DEVICE.guidance: Feature-detect it, or use the native modules for capability the web does not have.

WEB_OBSERVER.message: This observer is not implemented; only ResizeObserver is.
WEB_OBSERVER.guidance: Read geometry in a requestAnimationFrame callback, or observe the element's size instead.

WEB_STYLE.message: This part of CSSOM is not implemented; a sheet's rules are its source text.
WEB_STYLE.guidance: Insert or delete a whole rule through the sheet of a <style> element, and read values back with getComputedStyle.

WEB_COMPONENTS.message: Custom elements and shadow DOM are not implemented; DOMParser is.
WEB_COMPONENTS.guidance: Render with ordinary elements the bundler already emits.

WEB_TRANSFER.message: This part of DataTransfer is not implemented; a dropped file is a path, not a File.
WEB_TRANSFER.guidance: Read `event.dataTransfer.paths` and open each absolute path with your filesystem library. `types` still contains "Files", so the check that decides whether to accept a drop is unchanged. `setDragImage` draws for a drag out of the window, which cannot be started.

WEB_SELECTION.message: This part of the range API is not implemented; the boundary, text and geometry reads are.
WEB_SELECTION.guidance: Edit the tree with the node methods rather than through a range: a range here measures and compares, and does not cut.

usage.message: fetch names a path this application does not ship, and there is no server behind it.
usage.guidance: Ship the file in the output, or request an absolute http(s) URL.

usage.message: localStorage is in memory only: what it stores is gone when the application exits.
usage.guidance: Keep anything that must survive a restart in a file the application owns.

renderer.message: A property named by `transition` keeps its pre-stylesheet value (Blitz bug 689).
renderer.guidance: Inline the rule in a <style> element, or drop the transition, until it is fixed.

renderer.message: Fixed and sticky boxes resolve against the root box, not the viewport (Blitz bug 690).
renderer.guidance: Use normal, flex, grid, or bounded absolute layout for anything that must be placed exactly.

renderer.message: This paint effect is ignored rather than applied.
renderer.guidance: Check the element is still legible without it; use borders and backgrounds where it is not.

renderer.message: This document loads source, not built output; nothing in Blitsen transpiles it.
renderer.guidance: Run your bundler (Vite: `vite build`) and point Blitsen at its output directory.

renderer.message: Video and text tracks are not implemented; <audio> is.
renderer.guidance: Ship moving pictures as DOM, images and CSS, or feature-detect the media path.

renderer.message: This SVG feature does not paint; shapes, paths, text, gradients and clipPath do.
renderer.guidance: Flatten the effect into the shapes themselves, or rasterise this asset to PNG. A `<pattern>` fill also leaves a red mark in the frame's corner, so it is worth removing rather than tolerating.

assets.message: A remote <script src> is not fetched; it is skipped and the rest of the page runs.
assets.guidance: Bundle the script into the output directory and reference its local path.

assets.message: A remote asset is not part of a self-contained export; the request is answered with nothing.
assets.guidance: Bundle the asset into the output directory and reference its local path, and check the page still reads without it.

assets.message: A remote asset is not part of a self-contained export; the request is answered with nothing.
assets.guidance: Bundle the asset into the output directory and reference its local path, and check the page still reads without it.
